subject: Runway stabilization request — go-live risk and decision grid
messages:
From: Ari Shah <ari@medica.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2024 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Runway stabilization request — go-live risk

Camila,

We ran into a procurement gating issue overnight — our security team just flagged one of the third-party connectors for additional review and legal has asked for a revised data handling appendix. That pushes our ability to sign and accept the full integration beyond the 9/1 go-live target unless we accept a scoped, phased acceptance.

Quick ask: can Redwood provide a short MAP (mutual action plan) that splits the deliverables into an "integration baseline" we can accept on 9/1 and a follow-on acceptance window for the connector once legal finishes review? If we can get a firm decision grid with owner names and dates by EOD 8/15, procurement can try to accelerate the review. Otherwise we may need to push the go-live.

Appreciate any flexibility — Ari
Ari Shah
Director, Platform Integrations
Medica Health Systems

----
Ari attached: failing-connector-log.txt (stanza stub)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Ari Shah <ari@medica.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2024 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runway stabilization request — go-live risk

Thanks Ari — and sorry to hear about the late flag. We can do a short MAP that confines the 9/1 acceptance to the core inference integration (API + tokenization + KV cache behavior) while making the connector an explicit follow-on milestone.

Attached: proposed-map-v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria) and timeline-risk-log.csv (token-level impact estimates). Key points:
- Split acceptance: Core acceptance (M1) by 2024-09-01; Connector acceptance (M2) by 2024-10-15.
- Escalation lane: if procurement/legal do not sign M2 by 2024-09-22, we trigger the contingency (canary offload + temporary route to our hosted sandbox) — reduces initial scope but preserves core SLA.
- Owners: Camila (integration owner), Ben Carter (procurement liaison), Hannah Schmitt (ops escalation).

Can procurement confirm by 8/15 whether they can complete the connector review by 9/22? If not, we'll prepare a formal re-baseline and credit cadence for the follow-on window.

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-map-v2.xlsx, timeline-risk-log.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2024 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runway stabilization request — go-live risk

Camila — thanks for drafting the MAP. Tactical notes:
- Procurement often needs a single named approver from Legal to finish the connector appendix; if Medica can surface that name we can loop Legal at Redwood and chase parallel reviews.
- From a commercial perspective, propose a limited credit holdback tied to M2 (5% of the first three months' invoice) instead of delaying M1. That keeps revenue recognition aligned while giving Medica protection.
- Hannah, can we confirm capacity to spin the canary (sandbox route) by 8/28 if needed?

I'll step this up to Lauren for executive sign-off on the credit guardband and to coordinate the escalation email to procurement.

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Success Operations
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procure@acme.com>, ops@acme.com <ops@acme.com>, Ari Shah <ari@medica.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2024 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: decision required for MAP segmentation and acceptance windows (DEAL-8421)

Ari / Procurement —

Looping in executive procurement oversight so we can finalize the split acceptance approach. We propose the following decision grid:
- Option A (preferred): Accept M1 (core integration) on 2024-09-01, commit to M2 by 2024-10-15, with a 5% credit holdback applied to months 1–3 if M2 is delayed beyond 2024-10-22.
- Option B: Delay single-phase acceptance to 2024-10-15 (full scope). No holdback, but go-live deferred.

Please confirm Option A or B by COB 2024-08-20. If you select A but cannot provide Legal approver by 2024-08-15, we will proceed with an interim canary that preserves core functionality and a documented fallthrough plan.

Attached: escalation-approval-form.pdf (signature requested)

If we do not hear back by the deadline, Redwood will deem Option A accepted with the contingency plan described and will move forward with the canary on 8/28. This is to avoid a complete schedule slip that materially impacts other customers.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Partnerships & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

----
Forwarded message included below as a reference.

From: Ari Shah <ari@medica.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2024 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: decision required for MAP segmentation and acceptance windows (DEAL-8421)

Lauren / team —

Thanks for the clear options and the escalation path. Procurement confirms they cannot sign the connector appendix by 8/15 (internal resourcing), but they can commit to the Legal approver by 8/22 and aim to complete M2 by 10/15. Procurement requests the 5% holdback approach rather than a full delay — they prefer Option A.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood confirm the exact rollback plan if the connector fails final validation (how long will canary routing remain active and what are the latency implications)?
2) Can we cap any potential overage costs associated with the temporary hosted fallback to a $7,500 monthly ceiling while M2 is pending?

If you can add those two items to the MAP and provide an updated timeline by 8/18, we will sign Option A and return the escalation-approval-form.pdf with a named approver.

Appreciate the quick coordination — Ari
